newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate falls, baht stronger late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate falls, baht stronger late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate rose further to 8.25-8.50 percent in late trade on Wednesday from 7.50 percent early on tighter liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said the money supply was lower today due to mid-month value added tax payments and heavy buying of the dollar over the past few days.
The baht was higher to 25.482-25.487 to the dollar late from 25.484-25.488 earlier, dealers said.
"There was still strong bids for the dollar today. But some dollar selling interest emerged in the afternoon as the U.S. unit was down slightly abroad," one currency dealer said.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was quoted at 7.50/8.50 satangs per dollar late compared with 7.50/8.00 in early morning trade.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.47 to the dollar. The rate was the lowest level since January 31, 1994 when the mid-rate was set at 25.48.
